stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and evaluation of a significant large language model (LLM).

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Inside Microsoft’s big Copilot rethink
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is strategically repositioning Copilot as the 'OS for work' in its latest overhaul.
The announcement was made via an exclusive, invite-only event targeting key enterprise customers, signaling a B2B focus.
The shift suggests a deeper integration of AI into core enterprise workflows rather than just feature additions.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The tags confirm its association with major AI frameworks like transformers and the Llama family.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool use on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: AI music maker Suno now generates spoken words
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Suno, an AI music generator, has expanded its capabilities to include spoken word generation.
The new feature allows users to create voiceovers based on scripts or prompts, which can be paired with background music.
The functionality is currently available in public beta across Suno's web and mobile platforms.

stories.title: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Google is launching 'Guided Vision' within Gemini Live on compatible Android devices.
The feature uses AI to provide real-time audio descriptions of objects pointed at by the camera.
Key use cases include reading small text and identifying surroundings.

stories.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Federal judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits against Google concerning its AI Overviews.
The lawsuits, filed by Chegg and Penske Media, alleged Google was driving away web traffic with its AI search features.
Judge Amit Mehta ruled in Google's favor regarding the antitrust claims.

stories.title: Sony brings AI graphics upscaling to the regular PS5
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Sony is integrating a new AI upscaling technology, Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), into the standard PS5.
The technology is described as a 'new performance tier of AI upscaling' and is the result of Sony's Project Amethyst collaboration with AMD.
This update represents a significant step in leveraging AI for graphical enhancements on mainstream console hardware.

stories.title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Federal government cybersecurity has experienced a significant downturn recently.
Multiple hacks targeting two different federal agencies occurred within a single month.
These security breaches resulted in the exposure of a substantial amount of sensitive data.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of real-time animation for 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex avatar animations using linear combinations of blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a more efficient, shallow coefficient predictor for faster rendering.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level agentic tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Features 'runtime-free verifiable rewards,' suggesting a novel method for assessing command correctness without needing full execution in a live environment.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous self-improvement in embodied agents (robots).
Allows robots to improve execution capabilities without requiring updates to the core model weights.
The framework uses offline datasets to identify skills and generates simulated practice tasks based on execution feedback.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to unlock reasoning potential in multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities.
The system maintains a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve past environmental observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of real-time animation for 3D Gaussian avatars.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation) to replace heavy neural inference.
Achieves animation by approximating complex motion using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical gap: determining if LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool for probing LLM capabilities.
The findings aim to systematically diagnose mathematical weaknesses in LLMs to inform and improve post-training techniques.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
Decision models process text to provide probabilistic answers regarding yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden support for various models across different hardware.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Apple’s reportedly developing a smart home camera that doesn’t record video
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly developing a new smart home security camera.
The camera is rumored to function without recording video, instead providing text event descriptions.
This device is expected to be part of a broader, new Apple smart home ecosystem.

stories.title: Steam Deck 2: Is AMD Gainsborough the chip Valve’s been waiting for?
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The Steam Deck is aging, leading to high anticipation for a Steam Deck 2.
Valve has indicated the sequel requires a significant generational leap in performance and efficiency.
There is emerging speculation that AMD's Gainsborough chip may be the breakthrough component Valve is seeking.

stories.title: Can VR glasses save VR?
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has released new VR glasses, signaling a potential shift in the VR market.
The high price point ($1,299) is noted as a barrier to mass consumer adoption.
The hardware is described as a significant advancement over previous VR glasses.

stories.title: Judge dismisses Chegg and Penske antitrust lawsuits targeting Google AI search
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits filed by Chegg and Penske against Google regarding its AI search.
The court ruled that the issues surrounding AI search are not classified as antitrust violations.
The ruling acknowledges that AI search technology inherently carries certain consequences.

stories.title: Memory executives expect RAM shortage to continue through 2028
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Memory executives forecast that RAM shortages are expected to persist until 2028.
The trend indicates that memory prices for 2027 are projected to be significantly higher than those in 2026.
This suggests sustained supply chain constraints or high demand within the semiconductor industry.

stories.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: The game Stratego, which involves hidden information, previously posed a significant challenge to AI systems.
A breakthrough was achieved by integrating a second neural network specifically designed to infer the identity of concealed pieces.
This demonstrates progress in AI's ability to handle complex strategic games with incomplete information.

stories.title: As US relations fray, Canada gets serious about its own launch industry
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Canada is intensifying its focus on developing a domestic launch industry.
The Canada Rocket Company is specifically targeting medium-lift launch capabilities.
The push is occurring amid a backdrop of deteriorating US-Canada relations.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test an AI's ability to find inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages human expertise by having researchers annotate which past works influenced their current projects.
This addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to sense relevant, buried ideas within massive scientific archives.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces SILSA, a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation.
Addresses limitations of current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
Uses 'sliding-window slice latents' to represent shapes compactly while preserving topology.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) are proposed as an alternative to traditional autoregressive models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independence bottleneck found in discrete diffusion models during parallel decoding.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which allows for capturing statistical dependencies among tokens.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: Introduces DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) for fast visual generation.
DMAD reframes distribution matching as a classification task to learn log-density ratios directly.
It aims to improve upon existing methods by reducing the auxiliary memory and computation cost associated with traditional distribution matching.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to improve molecular learning models.
Addresses the limitation of standard sequential/graph formalisms in encoding complex molecular topology (e.g., ring systems).
Aims to provide a principled, topology-aware framework that is computationally feasible compared to existing high-order methods.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core method involves training a Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) model to forecast subsequent continuous embeddings.
This approach leverages the sequential nature of image generation (noisy to clean) to train the predictive model.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA is a new framework addressing limitations in high-resolution 3D generation methods.
It replaces fragmented voxel latents with compact, topology-aware sliding-window slice latents.
The goal is to improve topological consistency and reduce generation costs compared to existing multi-stage pipelines.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO is a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
It addresses the memory bottleneck caused by optimizer state, which limits the size of LLMs that can be trained on current GPUs.
TACO offers an alternative to existing methods (like state compression or geometry changes) and aims to maintain performance comparable to AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The paper presents an exact solution for cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs.
It replaces complex learned control mechanisms (like temporal-difference penalties) with a simpler Feynman-Kac tilt.
This mathematical simplification allows the cost-augmented bridge to be computed exactly against a tilted reference process.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models overcome this by denoising a shared continuous state, aiming to maintain inter-token statistical relationships.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale neural network optimization for LLMs.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size selection.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level agentic tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Emphasizes the importance of fine-grained, runtime-free verification due to the strict syntax requirements of cybersecurity command-line interfaces.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to identify inspiring prior research.
The benchmark leverages human expertise, using researchers to annotate which past papers influenced their current work.
The research addresses a key gap in AI: the ability to sense relevant, foundational ideas buried in vast scientific literature.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) are proposed as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independence issue in discrete models, where parallel decoding severs statistical dependencies.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which allows for better handling of bidirectional reasoning and global constraints.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Introduces AutoCompact, a method to train coding agents to intelligently manage context in long-horizon software engineering tasks.
Addresses the challenge that early context in long coding trajectories becomes stale, requiring agents to decide when and how to compact state.
The agent learns a policy to determine when to compact, what state to preserve, and how to resume work effectively.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can falsely credit small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
The paper proposes a 'cheap diagnostic ladder' to provide stricter evaluation for tool-use claims in smaller models.
The study demonstrates false positives using matched-architecture Spanish security language models, highlighting evaluation limitations.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new finetuning technique involving 'Sampling' to improve frontier models.
It challenges the conventional view that Reinforcement Learning (RL) is superior to Supervised Finetuning (SFT) for generalization.
The research explores the trade-offs between SFT's ability to use off-policy data versus RL's reliance on self-discovery.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench introduces a new evaluation framework for Data Agents designed for complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by supervising student models using privileged information from a teacher model.
It addresses a gap in current research where MLLM distillation has largely ignored this self-supervision approach, unlike recent methods focusing only on visual crops.

stories.title: Several vulnerabilities have been discovered in the Linux kernel
stories.author: luispa
bullet_points: Vulnerabilities have been found within the Linux kernel.
Kernel vulnerabilities represent a significant security risk to operating systems.
This is a critical topic for system administrators and security professionals.

stories.title: Clef: Open-weight decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
stories.author: jasondavies
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Clef,' an open-weight decision models framework.
The announcement includes a new platform specifically designed for Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
The focus is on democratizing access to advanced decision-making AI through open weights.
